messages.author: 8d044496e1ba6693
messages.subject: Using "group.label" changes results of CFA
parts:
Hi all,

I noticed that swapping the orders of groups when testing weak measurement invariance in a dataset where the factor loadings are not equal across groups changes the estimated factor loadings. Specifically, the estimates are "pulled" towards the data generating values of the group that serves as the reference group. I assumed the results would be equal, no matter which group is analyzed first (shows up in the dataset first).
Is this behaviour intended? Or am I doing something wrong/misunderstanding something? It worries me a bit because right now the results of my analysis change depending on the order of the observations in the dataset (which group shows up first).

Here is the code I used:
library(MASS)
library(lavaan)

set.seed(123)
nobs = 10000

#### generate factor scores ####
phi <- matrix(c(1, .5, .5, 1), ncol = 2) # factor (co)variances, identical across groups
alpha <- c(0, 0) # factor means, identical across groups

eta1 <- mvrnorm(nobs, mu = alpha, Sigma = phi, empirical=T) # generate factor scores group 1
eta2 <- mvrnorm(nobs, mu = alpha, Sigma = phi, empirical=T) # generate factor scores group 2

#### prepare matrices (standardized loadings) ####
## group 1
loadings1_fac1 <- c(.6, .5, .8, .9, .9)
loadings1_fac2 <- c(.5, .7, .9, .8, .8)
lambda1 <- matrix(c(loadings1_fac1, rep(0, 5), rep(0, 5), loadings1_fac2), nrow = 10, ncol = 2) # prepare loadings matrix
errorvar1 <- as.vector(c(1 - loadings1_fac1^2, 1 - loadings1_fac2^2)) # compute error variances
theta1 <- matrix(0, nrow = 10, ncol = 10) # create error covariance matrix
diag(theta1) <- errorvar1 # impute error variances on theta diagonal (assuming uncorrelated errors)

## group 2
loadings2_fac1 <- c(.6, .5, .8, .4, .4)
loadings2_fac2 <- c(.5, .7, .9, .3, .3)
lambda2 <- matrix(c(loadings2_fac1, rep(0, 5), rep(0, 5), loadings2_fac2), nrow = 10, ncol = 2) # prepare loadings matrix
errorvar2 <- as.vector(c(1 - loadings2_fac1^2, 1 - loadings2_fac2^2)) # compute error variances
theta2 <- matrix(0, nrow = 10, ncol = 10) # create error covariance matrix
diag(theta2) <- errorvar2 # impute error variances on theta diagonal (assuming uncorrelated errors)

#### generate errors and then observed scores (without intercepts) ####
epsilon1 <- mvrnorm(nrow(eta1), mu = rep(0, 10), Sigma = theta1, empirical=T) # errors in group 1
epsilon2 <- mvrnorm(nrow(eta2), mu = rep(0, 10), Sigma = theta2, empirical=T) # errors in group 2


df.1 <- as.data.frame(eta1 %*% t(lambda1) + epsilon1) # generate indicator scores in group 1
df.2 <- as.data.frame(eta2 %*% t(lambda2) + epsilon2) # generate indicator scores in group 2
df.1$group <- 1 # add grouping variable
df.2$group <- 2 # add grouping variable
df <- rbind(df.1, df.2) # combine the two dataframes

#### analyze the data ####
model <- "
    f1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5
    f2 =~ V6 + V7 + V8 + V9 + V10
    "

fit1 <- cfa(model, data = df, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE,
            group = "group", group.equal = c("loadings"))

fit2 <- cfa(model, data = df, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE,
           group = "group", group.equal = c("loadings"), group.label = c("2", "1"))

lavInspect(fit1, what = "est")$'1'$lambda
lavInspect(fit2, what = "est")$'1'$lambda
# the estimated factor loadings are not equal across the two fit objects

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Using "group.label" changes results of CFA
parts:
You are seeing the effect of std.lv = TRUE, which fixes the latent
variances to unity in the *first* group (only) when group.equal =
"loadings", but allows them to be free in the remaining groups.

As a result, switching the groups results in a different scale that is
used. Note that the standardized solutions are identical:

lavInspect(fit1, "std")$`1`$lambda
lavInspect(fit2, "std")$`1`$lambda

Yves.
